claims.claim: MT is arguably the strongest in vivo marker of myelin based on its spatial correspondence with myelin basic protein.
claims.source: While correlated with alternative myelin-sensitive imaging, MT is arguably the strongest in vivo marker of myelin, based on its spatial correspondence with myelin basic protein (Whitaker et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Comparative claim supported by citation.

claims.claim: Recent studies confirmed associations between adolescence and changes in myelin-markers.
claims.source: While recent studies confirmed associations between adolescence and changes in myelin-markers (Carey et al., 2018; Grydeland et al., 2019; Kwon et al., 2018; Whitaker et al., 2016), findings have been mainly cross-sectional, precluding inferences on intra-individual trajectories.
claims.evidence: Supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: Previous myelin-marker studies have been mainly cross-sectional, precluding inferences on intra-individual trajectories.
claims.source: While recent studies confirmed associations between adolescence and changes in myelin-markers (Carey et al., 2018; Grydeland et al., 2019; Kwon et al., 2018; Whitaker et al., 2016), findings have been mainly cross-sectional, precluding inferences on intra-individual trajectories.
claims.evidence: Limitation of prior work stated with citations.

claims.claim: Previous studies have generally focused on specific depths or intracortical averages, ignoring depth-dependent dynamics.
claims.source: Furthermore, studies have generally focused on specific depths or intracortical averages, ignoring depth-dependent dynamics and thus not addressing potential systematic shifts in cortical myeloarchitecture and lamination in adolescence.
claims.evidence: Critique of prior literature based on review.

claims.claim: Quantitative profiling of intracortical properties using central moments has been proposed to characterise cytoarchitecture in seminal histological work.
claims.source: Quantitative profiling of intracortical properties across cortical depths, and specifically parameterization using central moments (Papoulis and Unnikrishna Pillai, 2002), has been proposed to characterise cytoarchitecture in seminal histological work (Schleicher et al., 1999) and capture inter-individual variation (Amunts et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to methodological papers.

claims.claim: The mean (first moment) of MT profiles allows inferences on overall myelin content.
claims.source: In essence, studying the mean (first moment) of MT profiles perpendicular to the cortical mantle allows inferences on overall myelin content while higher order moments can address depth-dependent changes (Figure 1).
claims.evidence: Methodological interpretation with figure reference.

claims.claim: Higher order moments can address depth-dependent changes in MT profiles.
claims.source: In essence, studying the mean (first moment) of MT profiles perpendicular to the cortical mantle allows inferences on overall myelin content while higher order moments can address depth-dependent changes (Figure 1).
claims.evidence: Methodological interpretation with figure reference.

claims.claim: Analysis of skewness (third moment) can contrast relative properties of deep and superficial cortical layers.
claims.source: Analysis of skewness (third moment) can contrast relative properties of deep and superficial cortical layers, and depth is a critical dimension of laminar differentiation that relates to architectural complexity (Zilles et al., 2002) and cortical hierarchy (Mesulam, 1998).
claims.evidence: Methodological interpretation supported by citations.

claims.claim: Depth is a critical dimension of laminar differentiation that relates to architectural complexity and cortical hierarchy.
claims.source: Analysis of skewness (third moment) can contrast relative properties of deep and superficial cortical layers, and depth is a critical dimension of laminar differentiation that relates to architectural complexity (Zilles et al., 2002) and cortical hierarchy (Mesulam, 1998).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claims.claim: Classical histological findings showed overall increases in cortical myelin in adolescence.
claims.source: Applied to adolescence, such an analysis offers a non-invasive window into cortical architecture, which may recapitulate and expand classical histological findings showing overall increases in cortical myelin in adolescence (Kaes, 1907) as well as transcriptional analyses suggesting that laminar signatures reflect cortical development (Miller et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to classical work.

claims.claim: Transcriptional analyses suggest that laminar signatures reflect cortical development.
claims.source: Applied to adolescence, such an analysis offers a non-invasive window into cortical architecture, which may recapitulate and expand classical histological findings showing overall increases in cortical myelin in adolescence (Kaes, 1907) as well as transcriptional analyses suggesting that laminar signatures reflect cortical development (Miller et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation.

claims.claim: Microstructure profile covariance (MPC) quantifies inter-regional similarity in microstructure at a single subject-level.
claims.source: One such approach, known as microstructure profile covariance (MPC), quantifies inter-regional similarity in microstructure at a single subject-level (Paquola et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Methodological description supported by citation.

claims.claim: MPC has demonstrated utility for understanding large-scale patterns of cortical architecture, illustrating a sensory-fugal gradient of microstructural differentiation.
claims.source: Previous research has demonstrated the utility of MPC for understanding large-scale patterns of cortical architecture, specifically illustrating a sensory-fugal gradient of microstructural differentiation in both post mortem and in vivo datasets (Paquola et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: The sensory-fugal gradient describes gradual transitions from primary sensory and motor regions with high laminar differentiation through association cortex toward paralimbic areas with increasingly dysgranular appearance.
claims.source: This axis describes gradual transitions from primary sensory and motor regions with high laminar differentiation, through association cortex toward paralimbic areas with increasingly dysgranular appearance (Mesulam, 1998).
claims.evidence: Description supported by citation.

claims.claim: Microstructural similarity predicts cortico-cortical connectivity.
claims.source: Given prior evidence that microstructural similarity predicts cortico-cortical connectivity (Barbas and Rempel-Clower, 1997), tracking age-related changes in MPC provides an unprecedented way to probe coordinated maturation of microstructural networks during the critical adolescent period, moving towards a network perspective of structural brain development (Alexander-Bloch et al., 2013; Váša et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation.

claims.claim: The cortex-wide average MT profile shows a non-linear increase in intensity from superficial layers towards deeper layers.
claims.source: At baseline (i.e., using the average across timepoint 1), the cortex-wide average MT profile shows a non-linear increase in intensity from the superficial layers, adjacent to the pial boundary, towards the deeper layers approaching the white matter boundary, consistent with prior literature (Whitaker et al., 2016; Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: Baseline finding supported by citation and figure.

claims.claim: MT profiles show similar variations in mean and skewness across levels of laminar differentiation as post mortem myelin stained sections.
claims.source: Although post mortem myelin stained sections and in vivo MT profiles differ in terms of resolution and specificity to myelin, we observed similar variations in mean and skewness of profiles across levels of laminar differentiation (Figure 1B), supporting the extension of profile analysis from histology to in vivo MT imaging.
claims.evidence: Comparison finding with figure reference.

claims.claim: Mean MT was highest in idiotypic cortex and decreased with less laminar differentiation.
claims.source: At a whole cortex-level, mean MT was highest in idiotypic cortex and decreased with less laminar differentiation, while skewness exhibited an opposite pattern (spatial correlation = −0.23, pspin <0.001; Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplements 1–2, Appendix 1—figure 1).
claims.evidence: Baseline finding with statistical support and figure references.

claims.claim: Skewness exhibited an opposite pattern to mean MT across levels of laminar differentiation.
claims.source: At a whole cortex-level, mean MT was highest in idiotypic cortex and decreased with less laminar differentiation, while skewness exhibited an opposite pattern (spatial correlation = −0.23, pspin <0.001; Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplements 1–2, Appendix 1—figure 1).
claims.evidence: Baseline finding with statistical support and figure references.

claims.claim: Negative or near-zero skewness was observed in idiotypic and unimodal areas, relating to more even distribution of MT across cortical depths.
claims.source: Negative or near-zero skewness was observed in idiotypic and unimodal areas, relating to more even distribution of MT across cortical depths, whereas more positive skewness was observed in heteromodal and paralimbic areas, related to higher MT intensities in infragranular compared to supragranular layers (Zilles et al., 2002; Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: Baseline finding with citation and figure reference.

claims.claim: More positive skewness was observed in heteromodal and paralimbic areas, related to higher MT intensities in infragranular compared to supragranular layers.
claims.source: Negative or near-zero skewness was observed in idiotypic and unimodal areas, relating to more even distribution of MT across cortical depths, whereas more positive skewness was observed in heteromodal and paralimbic areas, related to higher MT intensities in infragranular compared to supragranular layers (Zilles et al., 2002; Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: Baseline finding with citation and figure reference.

claims.claim: The first principal gradient of MPC was anchored on one end by idiotypic sensory regions and by paralimbic regions on the other end.
claims.source: In line with previous work (Paquola et al., 2019), the first principal gradient within the baseline cohort was anchored on one end by idiotypic sensory regions and by paralimbic regions on the other end.
claims.evidence: Baseline finding supported by citation.

claims.claim: The sensory-fugal gradient was strongly correlated with MT profile skewness (r = 0.91, pspin <0.001).
claims.source: This sensory-fugal gradient reflects systematic variations in the MT profiles; it was strongly correlated with MT profile skewness (r = 0.91, pspin <0.001; Figure 1D) and weakly with mean MT (r = 0.19, pspin <0.001).
claims.evidence: Statistical finding with figure reference.

claims.claim: The sensory-fugal gradient was weakly correlated with mean MT (r = 0.19, pspin <0.001).
claims.source: This sensory-fugal gradient reflects systematic variations in the MT profiles; it was strongly correlated with MT profile skewness (r = 0.91, pspin <0.001; Figure 1D) and weakly with mean MT (r = 0.19, pspin <0.001).
claims.evidence: Statistical finding with figure reference.

claims.claim: Adolescence led to a significant increase in mean MT (qFDR <0.00625, % rate of change: [4.8 14.7] 95% CIs).
claims.source: Studying age-related changes in MT moments, we observed that adolescence led to a significant increase in the mean (qFDR <0.00625, % rate of change: [4.8 14.7] 95% CIs; Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1), suggesting overall increases in intracortical myelin content.
claims.evidence: Primary longitudinal finding with statistical support and figure references.

claims.claim: Adolescence led to decreases in skewness (qFDR <0.00625, % rate of change: [−179.2–34.6] 95% CIs).
claims.source: Conversely, we observed a unique spatial pattern of decreases in skewness (qFDR <0.00625, % rate of change: [−179.2–34.6] 95% CIs; Figure 2).
claims.evidence: Primary longitudinal finding with statistical support and figure reference.

claims.claim: Decreases in skewness reflected preferential increases in MT in mid to deeper layers.
claims.source: Depth-wise changes in MT intensity suggest that these decreases in skewness reflected a preferential increases in MT in mid to deeper layers, suggesting accumulation in myelin.
claims.evidence: Interpretation of depth-wise data.

claims.claim: Controlling for overall mean MT trajectories resulted in virtually identical patterns of skewness change.
claims.source: Controlling for overall mean MT trajectories resulted in virtually identical patterns of skewness change, suggesting relative independence between skewness and mean MT trajectories in adolescence (Appendix 1—figures 2–4).
claims.evidence: Control analysis finding with figure references.

claims.claim: Age-related changes in skewness were preferentially located in heteromodal (z > 3.06, p<0.043) and unimodal cortex (z > 3.24, p<0.024).
claims.source: Across all moments, age-related changes in skewness were preferentially located in heteromodal (z > 3.06, p<0.043) and unimodal cortex (z > 3.24, p<0.024), while idiotypic nodes were less prominently represented than expected by chance (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: Statistical finding with figure and supplementary file references.

claims.claim: Idiotypic nodes were less prominently represented in age-related skewness changes than expected by chance.
claims.source: Across all moments, age-related changes in skewness were preferentially located in heteromodal (z > 3.06, p<0.043) and unimodal cortex (z > 3.24, p<0.024), while idiotypic nodes were less prominently represented than expected by chance (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: Statistical finding with figure and supplementary file references.

claims.claim: The spatial distribution of MT profile mean and skewness were virtually unchanged when controlled for morphological and intensity confounds (r > 0.99).
claims.source: To this end, we computed residual MT moments by controlling for thickness or interface blurring at each vertex within node-wise linear models. The spatial distribution of MT profile mean and skewness were virtually unchanged when data were additionally controlled for morphological and intensity confounds (r > 0.99; Appendix 1—figures 2–4).
claims.evidence: Control analysis finding with figure references.

claims.claim: Age-related changes in MT moments were virtually identical when using MT profile data corrected for cortical thickness and interface blurring (r > 0.98).
claims.source: Age-related changes in MT moments were also virtually identical when using MT profile data corrected for cortical thickness and interface blurring (r > 0.98, Appendix 1—figures 2–4), supporting that MT profile trajectories were primarily driven by intracortical factors.
claims.evidence: Control analysis finding with figure references.

claims.claim: MT moments were relatively independent of regional variations in laminar thickness derived from post mortem volumetric reconstruction (mean: −0.06 < r < 0.05. skewness: −0.17 < r < 0.02).
claims.source: Furthermore, spatial correlations suggested that MT moments were relatively independent of regional variations in laminar thickness derived from a post mortem volumetric reconstruction of a Merker-stained human brain (Wagstyl et al., 2018) (mean: −0.06 < r < 0.05. skewness: −0.17 < r < 0.02; Appendix 1—figure 5).
claims.evidence: Comparison analysis with citation and figure reference.

claims.claim: The pattern of age-related change in skewness showed enrichment exclusively with oligodendrocytes (p<0.001 at a specificity index threshold of 0.0001).
claims.source: Cell specific expression analysis (Dougherty et al., 2010) suggested enrichment exclusively with oligodendrocytes (p<0.001 [at a specificity index threshold of 0.0001]; Figure 3A), confirming the association between myelination and decreased MT skewness.
claims.evidence: Gene expression analysis finding with citation and figure reference.

claims.claim: Developmental expression analysis showed selective enrichment for adolescence and young adulthood.
claims.source: Developmental expression analysis (Dougherty et al., 2010) showed selective enrichment for adolescence and young adulthood (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: Gene expression analysis finding with citation and figure reference.

claims.claim: Gene ontology analysis indicated a negative association with demyelination (Z = −2.16, p=0.001) and axon degeneration (Z = −2.34, p=0.011).
claims.source: Furthermore, we performed gene ontology analysis using a modified Fishers exact test, which captures the deviation from the expected gene rank (Kuleshov et al., 2016), on genes associated with decreasing skewness. This indicated a negative association with demyelination (Z = −2.16, p=0.001) and axon degeneration (Z = −2.34, p=0.011), reinforcing associations to myelin.
claims.evidence: Gene ontology analysis finding with citation.

claims.claim: Genes negatively associated with age-related skewness reduction were less likely to be enriched for demyelination and were exclusively associated with oligodendrocytes.
claims.source: In sum, genes negatively associated with age-related skewness reduction were less likely to be enriched for demyelination and were exclusively associated with oligodendrocytes.
claims.evidence: Summary of gene expression findings.

claims.claim: MT skewness changes during adolescent development appear to be strongly reflective of changes in myelination.
claims.source: Thus, MT skewness changes during adolescent development appear to be strongly reflective of changes in myelination.
claims.evidence: Interpretation based on gene expression analyses.

claims.claim: Exploratory rank-based correlations indicated a small correlation between mean and skewness related genes (rho = 0.14, p<0.001).
claims.source: However, exploratory rank-based correlations on the weights of each gene indicated a small correlation between mean and skewness related genes (rho = 0.14, p<0.001), indicating mean and skewness share a modest transcriptomic signature.
claims.evidence: Statistical finding from gene expression analysis.

claims.claim: Baseline data analysis did not identify a whole genome transcriptional profile that overlapped with any of the baseline MT moments.
claims.source: Finally, it should be noted that the same analysis on baseline data only (average across a single scan per subject) from this cohort did not identify a whole genome transcriptional profile that overlapped with any of the baseline MT moments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), reinforcing the added value of developmental data (e.g. measuring an age-related change) in detecting human neurodevelopmental processes by myelin-sensitive MRI.
claims.evidence: Negative finding with figure reference.

claims.claim: At the edge-level, adolescent development was primarily related to increases in MPC (1564 increases vs 534 decreases at qFDR <0.025).
claims.source: At the node-to-node edge-level, adolescent development was primarily related to increases in MPC (1564 increases vs 534 decreases at qFDR <0.025; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: MPC analysis finding with figure reference.

claims.claim: The first principal component (G1DEV) illustrated a sensory-fugal gradient, explaining 33% variance.
claims.source: The first principal component (G1DEV) illustrated a sensory-fugal gradient, explaining 33% variance (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: Dimensionality reduction finding with figure reference.

claims.claim: Idiotypic sensory and motor areas became increasingly coupled in adolescence, and more segregated from paralimbic nodes.
claims.source: On one end of the gradient, idiotypic sensory and motor areas became increasingly coupled in adolescence, and more segregated from the opposite anchor constituted mainly of paralimbic nodes.
claims.evidence: Interpretation of gradient analysis.

claims.claim: The concordance of the developmental gradient (G1DEV) with the baseline MPC gradient (r = 0.89, p<0.001) suggested that the axis of microstructural differentiation expands during adolescence.
claims.source: The concordance of the developmental gradient (G1DEV) with the baseline MPC gradient (r = 0.89, p<0.001, Figure 1D) suggested that the axis of microstructural differentiation expands during adolescence.
claims.evidence: Statistical finding with interpretation and figure reference.

claims.claim: Heteromodal and unimodal cortex were drawn outwards towards one of the gradient anchors in older individuals.
claims.source: Heteromodal and unimodal cortex, occupying central regions of the gradient, were drawn outwards towards one of the gradient anchors in older individuals (Figure 4B), forming a more bimodal distribution (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: Age-strata comparison finding with figure references.

claims.claim: Prefrontal and medial parietal areas were increasingly coupled with sensory areas in older individuals.
claims.source: Specifically, prefrontal and medial parietal areas were increasingly coupled with sensory areas, and temporal regions increased in similarity to paralimbic regions (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: Age-strata comparison finding with figure reference.

claims.claim: Temporal regions increased in similarity to paralimbic regions in older individuals.
claims.source: Specifically, prefrontal and medial parietal areas were increasingly coupled with sensory areas, and temporal regions increased in similarity to paralimbic regions (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: Age-strata comparison finding with figure reference.

claims.claim: Greater decreases in MT skewness were related to sensory anchor coupling (r = −0.63, pspin <0.001).
claims.source: By relating the age-related shifts in MPC to anchors with age-related changes in MT moments, we found that greater decreases in MT skewness were related to sensory anchor coupling (r = −0.63, pspin <0.001; Figure 4C; Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: Correlation finding with figure references.

claims.claim: Restricted age-related skewness changes were associated with paralimbic anchor coupling (r = 0.65, pspin <0.001).
claims.source: Conversely, restricted age-related skewness changes were associated with paralimbic anchor coupling (r = 0.65, pspin <0.001).
claims.evidence: Correlation finding.

claims.claim: Depth-dependent myelination during adolescence reshapes myeloarchitecture and underpins macro-scale reorganisation of cortical networks.
claims.source: Together, these findings demonstrate how depth-dependent myelination during adolescence reshapes myeloarchitecture and underpins macro-scale reorganisation of cortical networks.
claims.evidence: Summary interpretation of findings.

claims.claim: Adolescent development was characterized by two developmental processes: one involving overall increases in mean MT and one involving preferential MT increases in mid-to-deeper cortical layers.
claims.source: Changes to intracortical myelin can be generally characterised by two developmental processes, one involving overall increases in mean MT and one involving preferential MT increases in mid-to-deeper cortical layers.
claims.evidence: Summary of primary findings.

claims.claim: Both developmental processes particularly affected unimodal and heteromodal association cortices.
claims.source: Both processes particularly affected unimodal and heteromodal association cortices that is areas between low-level sensory and motor areas on the one end of the cortical hierarchy and high-level transmodal and limbic regions on the other end.
claims.evidence: Summary of spatial findings.

claims.claim: Intracortical microstructural changes were independent from age-related effects on overall cortical morphology and tissue contrast.
claims.source: A series of complementary explorations, based on alternative neuroimaging features known to undergo large-scale changes in adolescence (Giedd et al., 2015; Raznahan et al., 2011; Sowell et al., 2004), demonstrated the independence of these intracortical microstructural changes from age-related effects on overall cortical morphology and tissue contrast.
claims.evidence: Summary of control analyses with citations.

claims.claim: Patterns of age-related change overlapped with genes associated with oligodendrocyte processes.
claims.source: In addition, cross-referencing our findings against post mortem gene expression maps showed that patterns of age-related change overlapped with genes associated with oligodendrocyte processes, supporting the specificity of MT changes to myelin.
claims.evidence: Summary of gene expression findings.

claims.claim: Local processes were paralleled by a cortex-wide differentiation along the sensory-fugal axis.
claims.source: Leveraging microstructure profile covariance analysis, we explored coordination of intracortical microstructure characteristics across distributed areas (Paquola et al., 2019). This showed that local processes were paralleled by a cortex-wide differentiation along the sensory-fugal axis.
claims.evidence: Summary of MPC findings with citation.

claims.claim: The sensory-fugal axis underpins the segregation of lower- from higher-order components of the putative cortical hierarchy.
claims.source: This axis ultimately underpins the segregation of lower- from higher-order components of the putative cortical hierarchy.
claims.evidence: Interpretation of gradient findings.

claims.claim: The skewness of the MT profile tilts from infragranular-dominant in paralimbic regions towards a more even distribution across cortical depths in sensory regions.
claims.source: The skewness of the MT profile, reflecting nonlinear increases in myelin towards deeper layers (Dinse et al., 2015; Sprooten et al., 2019; Waehnert et al., 2014), tilts from infragranular-dominant in paralimbic regions towards a more even distribution across cortical depths in sensory regions.
claims.evidence: Interpretation of baseline findings with citations.

claims.claim: The graded shift in skewness parallels changes in the laminar origin of projections.
claims.source: This graded shift parallels changes in the laminar origin of projections, where paralimbic regions engaged in feedback processing project from infragranular layers and sensory regions providing feedforward information project predominantly from supragranular layers (Felleman and Van Essen, 1991).
claims.evidence: Interpretation linking findings to known connectivity patterns with citation.

claims.claim: Mean myelin increased from polar towards sensory regions, recapitulating prior post mortem evidence and established atlases of cytoarchitecture.
claims.source: Meanwhile, mean myelin increased from polar towards sensory regions, recapitulating prior post mortem evidence (Vogt and Vogt, 1919; Vogt, 1911), established atlases of cytoarchitecture (Von Economo and Koskinas, 2008), and resting-state functional connectivity gradients (Hong et al., 2017; Margulies et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Baseline finding supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: Mean and skewness trajectories showed concomitant but independent developmental patterns.
claims.source: Tracking longitudinal change in intracortical MT profiles, we found concomitant but independent developmental patterns in the trajectory of mean and skewness.
claims.evidence: Summary of longitudinal findings.

claims.claim: Both mean and skewness changes were strongly and preferentially located in heteromodal and unimodal association cortex, yet they only partially overlapped.
claims.source: Both sets of age-related changes were strongly and preferentially located in heteromodal and unimodal association cortex; yet, they only partially overlapped, a finding also supported by gene expression analysis.
claims.evidence: Summary of spatial and gene expression findings.

claims.claim: Only skewness changes, but not mean MT changes, were spatially associated with oligodendrocyte gene expression patterns.
claims.source: Only skewness changes, but not mean MT changes, were spatially associated with oligodendrocyte gene expression patterns.
claims.evidence: Gene expression finding.

claims.claim: Skewness effects occurred independently of MRI-based measures of cortical interface blurring and variations in cortical thickness.
claims.source: Additional analyses indicated that skewness effects occurred rather independently of MRI-based measures of cortical interface blurring and variations in cortical thickness, supporting specificity to intracortical microstructure.
claims.evidence: Summary of control analyses.

claims.claim: Increasing mean MT likely reflects myelination of previously unmyelinated axons.
claims.source: Our findings may align with several mechanisms of experience-dependent myelination (de Faria et al., 2018). Increasing mean MT likely reflects myelination of previously unmyelinated axons.
claims.evidence: Interpretation with citation.

claims.claim: Skewness changes likely capture architectural reconfigurations or laminar specific changes in axonal myelination.
claims.source: On the other hand, as skewness changes persisted even after controlling for changes in the mean, these more likely capture architectural reconfigurations or laminar specific changes in axonal myelination.
claims.evidence: Interpretation based on control analyses.

claims.claim: Underlying mechanisms may include de novo generation of oligodendrocytes, activity-dependent modifications in neuronal and oligodendrocyte precursors, and tuning of the distance between nodes of Ranvier.
claims.source: Underlying mechanisms may include de novo generation of oligodendrocytes (Zuccaro and Arlotta, 2013), activity-dependent modifications in neuronal and oligodendrocyte precursors (Gibson et al., 2014), and tuning of the distance between nodes of Ranvier along both cortico-cortical as well as long-range axons (Arancibia-Cárcamo et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: Speculation about mechanisms supported by citations.

claims.claim: The putative functional role of myelin in cortical grey matter may be to insulate fibres from making new synaptic connections, thus enhancing stability.
claims.source: The putative functional role of myelin in cortical grey matter may be to insulate fibres from making new synaptic connections, thus enhancing stability (Braitenberg, 1962; Braitenberg and Schüz, 1998; Micheva et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Speculation about function supported by citations.

claims.claim: Overall lower myelin content in transmodal regions might indicate a higher potential for plasticity.
claims.source: Conversely, overall lower myelin content in transmodal regions might indicate a higher potential for plasticity (Huntenburg et al., 2017), possibly making these areas more suitable to support adaptive behaviour and learning that are core to many integrative functions that mature during adolescence.
claims.evidence: Speculation supported by citation.

claims.claim: Rodent experiments suggest that experience-induced oligodendrocyte remodelling supports the development of positive social behaviour.
claims.source: Rodent experiments suggest that experience-induced oligodendrocyte remodelling supports the development of positive social behaviour (Makinodan et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to animal studies.

claims.claim: Abnormal myelination has been implicated in several brain disorders.
claims.source: Conversely, abnormal myelination has been implicated in several brain disorders, however, studies on intracortical myeloarchitecture are scarce (Mighdoll et al., 2015; Stedehouder and Kushner, 2017; Bernhardt et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations.

claims.claim: The architectural changes observed may represent a microstructural substrate that could determine overall cognitive and social capacities or susceptibility to neuropsychiatric and neurological conditions.
claims.source: The architectural changes observed in the present cohort may represent a microstructural substrate that could determine overall cognitive and social capacities or susceptibility to a range of neuropsychiatric and neurological conditions occurring in late childhood and adolescence.
claims.evidence: Speculation about implications.

claims.claim: Decreases in MT profile skewness pushed regions to a more sensory-like architecture.
claims.source: Specifically, decreases in MT profile skewness pushed regions to a more sensory-like architecture (which was coupled with high mean MT).
claims.evidence: Interpretation of MPC findings.

claims.claim: Increases in skewness pushed regions towards a paralimbic-like MT profile.
claims.source: In contrast, increases in skewness pushed regions towards a paralimbic-like MT profile.
claims.evidence: Interpretation of MPC findings.

claims.claim: Two regionally distinct developmental patterns within the association cortex promoted a more bimodal distribution of myeloarchitectural types across the cortex.
claims.source: These two regionally distinct developmental patterns within the association cortex promoted a more bimodal distribution of myeloarchitectural types across the cortex.
claims.evidence: Summary interpretation of findings.

claims.claim: Similar properties of modular segregation in tractography-based networks have been shown to mediate age-related improvements in executive function throughout adolescence.
claims.source: Similar properties of modular segregation in tractography-based networks have been shown to mediate age-related improvements in executive function throughout adolescence (Baum et al., 2017), reinforcing the importance of these processes for understanding psychosocial maturation.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Drifts in association cortex towards either sensory-like or paralimbic-like architecture represents an expansion of the sensory-fugal gradient of microstructural differentiation.
claims.source: Drifts in association cortex towards either sensory-like or paralimbic-like architecture represents, thus, an expansion of the sensory-fugal gradient of microstructural differentiation (Paquola et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Interpretation with citation.

claims.claim: The sensory-fugal gradient was previously described by Mesulam based on non-human primate research to encapsulate cortex-wide variations in architecture and connectivity.
claims.source: Such a sensory-fugal gradient was previously described by Mesulam (1998) based on non-human primate research to encapsulate cortex-wide variations in architecture and connectivity, and has since been suggested to reflect increasing synaptic plasticity towards transmodal regions (García-Cabezas et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations.

claims.claim: Systematic variations in the degree of experience-dependent plasticity may explain why myelin-derived markers develop differently along the sensory-fugal gradient.
claims.source: Systematic variations in the degree of experience-dependent plasticity may explain why myelin-derived markers develop differently along the sensory-fugal gradient (de Faria et al., 2018), in contrast to other known developmental gradients such as the rostro-caudal timing of terminal neurogenesis (Rakic, 1974).
claims.evidence: Speculation supported by citations.

claims.claim: Differentiation of association cortices conforms with notions of the 'tethering hypothesis' of cortical evolution.
claims.source: Differentiation of association cortices also conforms with notions of the 'tethering hypothesis' of cortical evolution (Buckner and Krienen, 2013).
claims.evidence: Interpretation supported by citation.

claims.claim: According to the tethering hypothesis, intermediate regions of the cortical hierarchy are less constrained by extrinsic inputs and intrinsic signaling molecules, which has allowed for massive surface area expansion throughout mammalian evolution.
claims.source: According to this framework, intermediate regions of the cortical hierarchy are less constrained by extrinsic inputs and intrinsic signaling molecules, which has allowed for massive surface area expansion throughout mammalian evolution.
claims.evidence: Description of cited framework.

claims.claim: Reduced constraints on association cortices allow for protracted development of myeloarchitecture, whereas the sensory and limbic anchors are well-defined prior to adolescence.
claims.source: Our findings suggest that reduced constraints on association cortices allow for protracted development of myeloarchitecture, whereas the sensory and limbic anchors are well-defined prior to adolescence.
claims.evidence: Interpretation of findings in context of tethering hypothesis.

results.result: The study used an accelerated longitudinal cohort design with 180 adolescents and young adults (aged 14-27) scanned at two time points using magnetization transfer (MT) imaging to generate intracortical profiles.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C98-C103 collectively describe the study design, sample characteristics, and imaging methodology. The cohort design is well-documented with specific sample sizes (234 initially, 180 after quality control), age stratification, retention rates (74%), and technical acquisition details. The methodology is appropriately described with citations supporting the MT imaging approach.

results.result: Mixed-effect models revealed two independent developmental processes during adolescence: overall increases in mean MT and decreases in MT skewness (reflecting preferential increases in mid-to-deeper layers), both preferentially affecting heteromodal and unimodal association cortices.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C4, C41-C46, C67-C68 describe the primary longitudinal findings with appropriate statistical support (qFDR <0.00625, specific effect sizes with confidence intervals). The independence of the two processes is demonstrated through control analyses (C44), and spatial specificity is confirmed with permutation testing (C45-C46). The statistical approach using linear mixed-effect models is appropriate for the accelerated longitudinal design.

results.result: MT profile developmental changes were independent of morphological changes including cortical thickness and interface blurring, as demonstrated by control analyses showing virtually identical patterns when correcting for these confounds (r > 0.98-0.99).
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C47-C49, C69, C79 describe comprehensive control analyses demonstrating independence from morphological confounds. The high correlations (r > 0.98-0.99) between corrected and uncorrected data provide strong quantitative evidence. Additional validation against post-mortem laminar thickness data (C49) further supports specificity to intracortical microstructure rather than morphology.

results.result: Age-related changes in MT skewness spatially co-localized with oligodendrocyte gene expression markers, showing cell-type specific enrichment (p<0.001) and developmental enrichment for adolescence/young adulthood, with negative associations to demyelination processes.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C50-C54, C70, C78 describe gene expression validation analyses with appropriate statistical thresholds (pFDR <0.05, specificity index 0.0001). The cell-type specificity to oligodendrocytes and developmental timing enrichment provide biological validation. However, the authors appropriately acknowledge limitations: gene expression data are cross-sectional adult post-mortem samples, making developmental inferences indirect. The negative finding for baseline data (C56) strengthens the specificity of the longitudinal signal.

results.result: Microstructure profile covariance (MPC) analysis revealed that intracortical changes contributed to expansion of the sensory-fugal gradient, with heteromodal and unimodal cortices differentiating toward either sensory or paralimbic anchors, forming a more bimodal distribution in older individuals.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C57-C66, C71-C72 describe the MPC network analysis findings with appropriate statistical support. The developmental gradient (G1DEV) explained 33% variance and showed high concordance with baseline gradients (r=0.89). The relationship between MT moment changes and gradient shifts is quantified with significant correlations (r=-0.63 to 0.65, pspin <0.001). The analysis appropriately uses diffusion map embedding and Procrustes alignment for cross-sectional comparisons.

results.result: Baseline MT profiles showed non-linear increases from superficial to deeper layers, with mean MT highest in idiotypic cortex and skewness showing opposite patterns. MT profile variations corresponded to post-mortem myelin staining patterns and established cytoarchitectural gradients.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C40, C73, C75 describe baseline characterization with appropriate validation against histological data and prior literature. The spatial correlation between mean and skewness (r=-0.23, pspin <0.001) and strong correlation of the MPC gradient with skewness (r=0.91) provide quantitative support. Comparison with post-mortem myelin stains (C33) provides qualitative validation, though the authors appropriately acknowledge differences in resolution and specificity.

results.result: The mean (first moment) of MT profiles captures overall myelin content while skewness (third moment) captures depth-dependent changes contrasting deep versus superficial layers, based on established histological profiling methods.
results.evaluation: Claims C21-C25 describe the methodological framework with appropriate citations to histological work (Schleicher et al., 1999; Amunts et al., 1999; Zilles et al., 2002). The interpretation of moments is consistent with established statistical theory and prior cytoarchitectural applications. The biological interpretation linking depth to laminar differentiation and cortical hierarchy is well-supported by citations.

results.result: The equivolumetric surface-based approach provides better biological validity and precision than conventional voxel-based morphometry by accounting for cortical folding and reducing partial volume effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C106 describe methodological advantages with appropriate citations (Wagstyl et al., 2018; Waehnert et al., 2014; Ziegler et al., 2019). The equivolumetric approach is validated against post-mortem data in cited work. CSF correction using mixed tissue models (described in methods) addresses partial volume effects. The claims are appropriately framed as methodological improvements rather than absolute validation.

results.result: MT imaging is sensitive to myelin-related molecules and serves as a viable in vivo proxy for myelin basic protein, though it cannot be directly equated with cortical myelin content per se.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C17 appropriately characterize MT imaging with balanced discussion of strengths and limitations, supported by multiple citations. The authors correctly acknowledge that MT cannot be equated with myelin content (C14) while presenting evidence for its utility as a myelin proxy (C15-C17). The claim that MT is 'arguably the strongest' marker (C17) is appropriately hedged and citation-supported.

results.result: Mean and skewness-related genes showed modest transcriptomic overlap (rho=0.14, p<0.001), and baseline MT moments did not show significant whole-genome transcriptional associations, highlighting the value of longitudinal developmental data.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C56 describe exploratory and negative findings that strengthen the main gene expression results. The small correlation (rho=0.14) between mean and skewness gene signatures supports their independence. The negative baseline finding (C56) is important for demonstrating specificity of the developmental signal, though the authors appropriately note this reinforces rather than proves the developmental associations.

results.result: Mean and skewness trajectories showed concomitant but independent developmental patterns, both preferentially located in heteromodal and unimodal association cortex with only partial spatial overlap.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C77 summarize the relationship between the two developmental processes, supported by the detailed findings in other claim groups. The independence is demonstrated through control analyses (C44) and gene expression patterns (C78). The partial spatial overlap is consistent with the statistical findings showing both processes affect association cortices but with different spatial distributions.

results.result: The authors speculate that increasing mean MT reflects myelination of previously unmyelinated axons while skewness changes capture architectural reconfigurations or laminar-specific myelination changes, with potential implications for cognitive development and disease susceptibility.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C84, C87, C94, C97 are explicitly speculative interpretations about mechanisms and functional implications. While these speculations are appropriately hedged with language like 'likely,' 'may,' and 'might,' and are supported by citations to relevant literature, they extend beyond what the data directly demonstrate. The proposed mechanisms (C82) and functional roles (C83-C84) are plausible but not tested in this study. These remain hypotheses for future investigation.

results.result: Decreases in MT skewness pushed regions toward sensory-like architecture while increases pushed regions toward paralimbic-like profiles, promoting a more bimodal distribution and representing expansion of the sensory-fugal gradient.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C90, C92 interpret the MPC findings in terms of architectural differentiation. These interpretations are supported by the quantitative findings (C61-C65) showing differential shifts along the gradient and correlations between MT changes and anchor coupling. The bimodal distribution is documented in supplementary figures. The interpretation as gradient expansion is consistent with the high correlation between developmental and baseline gradients (C60).

results.result: Prior literature established that adolescence involves large-scale brain reconfigurations with regionally-variable cortical thinning, but previous myelin-marker studies were mainly cross-sectional and focused on specific depths rather than depth-dependent dynamics.
results.evaluation: Claims C8-C10, C18-C20 accurately summarize prior literature with appropriate citations. The characterization of limitations in prior work (C19-C20) provides appropriate context for the current study's contributions. These claims establish the rationale for the longitudinal, depth-dependent approach used in the current work.

results.result: The study builds on classical histological findings of adolescent myelin increases and extends frameworks including the sensory-fugal gradient concept and the tethering hypothesis of cortical evolution to understand adolescent myeloarchitectural development.
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C31, C93, C95-C96 appropriately contextualize the work within established theoretical frameworks, all supported by citations. The sensory-fugal gradient concept (Mesulam, 1998) and tethering hypothesis (Buckner & Krienen, 2013) provide interpretive frameworks for the findings. The authors appropriately distinguish between recapitulating classical findings (C26) and extending them with new in vivo longitudinal data.

results.result: Morphometric analyses typically only quantify cortical boundary changes and may not be specific for microstructural changes within the cortical mantle that are important for adolescent development.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C12 accurately characterize limitations of conventional morphometric approaches, supported by citation (Huntenburg et al., 2017). This provides appropriate motivation for the intracortical profiling approach. The limitation is well-established in the neuroimaging literature and the characterization is fair.

results.result: Prior work in rodents and humans suggests that oligodendrocyte remodeling supports social behavior development, abnormal myelination is implicated in brain disorders, and modular network segregation mediates executive function improvements in adolescence.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C86, C91 accurately cite prior literature to provide context for functional and clinical implications. These are appropriately presented as established findings from other studies rather than claims from the current work. The citations support the statements made.

results.result: The graded shift in MT skewness parallels changes in laminar origin of projections, where paralimbic regions project from infragranular layers and sensory regions project from supragranular layers.
results.evaluation: Claim C74 links the observed MT skewness gradient to known anatomical connectivity patterns, supported by citation (Felleman & Van Essen, 1991). This interpretation connects the microstructural findings to established principles of cortical organization. The parallel between skewness patterns and projection origins is a reasonable inference supported by the cited anatomical literature.
